en: Taal Volcano's main crater lake often changes color from green to white during periods of volcanic unrest.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The grass-covered Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate kisses.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape visible from many surrounding towns.
Lake Buhi in Camarines Sur is a shallow freshwater lake that hosts the world's smallest commercial fish.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea contains hundreds of coral species and diverse marine life.
The northeast monsoon, or amihan, brings cool and dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features exceptionally clear, deep blue freshwater flowing from an underwater cave.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into the mountains and follow the natural contours of the land.
A crater lake formed inside Mount Pinatubo's caldera after its massive 1991 eruption filled with rainwater.
Great Santa Cruz Island in Zamboanga City features a rare pink sand beach made from crushed red corals.
The Agusan Marsh Wildlife Sanctuary in Mindanao is the largest freshwater marshland in the Philippines, flooded year-round.
